text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000096 bills 99215 at well above the risk-adjusted expectation, with the excess concentrated in mid-to-high complexity patients, but only four documented 99215 claims make the documentation too thin to settle whether the higher coding is supported.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevated 99215 share is not driven mainly by low-complexity patients: rates on 0–1 condition visits sit near the all-provider rates, while the excess appears in patients with 2 or more conditions (for example C0053519, C0053659 and C0054275). That pattern is consistent with either a sicker-than-average panel within each complexity band or a habit of coding up on moderately complex visits, and the gap is largest in the 2–3 condition bands, where clinical judgment is most discretionary. The records review found no billed-above-documented claims at any level, and all four documented 99215s (including C0053998) show high MDM, but four charts out of 113 99215 claims cannot carry a conclusion. Only one of 19 moderate-plus data-reviewed notes lacked a lab line, so there is little sign of cloned documentation. A reviewer should first request a larger, targeted sample of 99215 charts, prioritizing the 2–3 condition visits and the low-complexity examples such as C0053965 (hypertension only) and C0054144 (no chronic conditions, URI diagnosis), to test whether the documented MDM supports the billed level."}
